system.name: 55 Cancri
system.description: A nearby star 41 light-years away hosting five planets, from a scorching super-Earth to a distant outer giant.

55cancri-star.name: 55 Cancri A
55cancri-star.description: 55 Cancri A is a yellow dwarf star located 41 light-years from Earth in the constellation Cancer. It is the primary star of a binary system and is slightly cooler and smaller than our Sun, hosting five confirmed exoplanets.
55cancri-star.funFact: 55 Cancri A has a red dwarf companion star (55 Cancri B) orbiting about 1,065 AU away, making this a binary star system.

55cancri-e.name: 55 Cancri e
55cancri-e.description: 55 Cancri e is a super-Earth that orbits its star in less than 18 hours, making it one of the shortest-period exoplanets known. The surface temperature is thought to exceed 2,000°C, hot enough to melt rock and potentially create lava oceans.
55cancri-e.funFact: 55 Cancri e has been nicknamed 'Janssen' and is sometimes called a 'lava world' — its surface may be entirely covered in molten rock.

55cancri-b.name: 55 Cancri b
55cancri-b.description: 55 Cancri b is a hot Jupiter that was the first of the system's planets to be discovered, found in 1996. Despite orbiting much closer than Jupiter does in our Solar System, it is a gas giant of comparable mass.
55cancri-b.funFact: 55 Cancri b was discovered using the radial velocity method, detecting the gravitational wobble it induces in its host star.

55cancri-c.name: 55 Cancri c
55cancri-c.description: 55 Cancri c is a Saturn-class planet orbiting in the system's middle region. Its mass is about half that of Saturn, and it may be a gas planet with a solid or liquid core.
55cancri-c.funFact: 55 Cancri c's orbital period of 44 days places it in a region where water could theoretically exist in some phases under the right atmospheric pressure.

55cancri-f.name: 55 Cancri f
55cancri-f.description: 55 Cancri f is a Neptune-class planet that orbits near the habitable zone of its star. It was discovered by the radial velocity method and represents a class of intermediate-mass planets between Neptune and Saturn.
55cancri-f.funFact: 55 Cancri f was once thought to be in the habitable zone of its star, sparking interest in whether any hypothetical moons could harbor liquid water.

55cancri-d.name: 55 Cancri d
55cancri-d.description: 55 Cancri d is a super-Jupiter orbiting far from the star with a period of about 14 Earth years. It is the most massive planet in the system and was the first to be discovered around 55 Cancri, found alongside b in 1996.
55cancri-d.funFact: 55 Cancri d is so massive — nearly four times Jupiter's mass — that it may have influenced the formation and orbits of the inner planets over billions of years.
